comment: Life-safety endpoints that must refuse over clearnet (ARCHITECTURE §9.2; CLAUDE.md §3 'Tor/.onion for life-safety flows'). Two IPs on one low-volume Durable Object inside the jitter window is a strong pairing that sealed-sender cannot hide, so the medical broker and the detainee handshakes are onion-only and refuse rather than degrade. gate-onion-only.mjs enforces three things per entry: the route exists, requireOnionOrigin runs INSIDE that route's own handler block and BEFORE any flag read, credential check or binding read, and a test names the endpoint and proves the 403.
inverse_comment: The rule also runs backwards: any handler in workers/** that calls requireOnionOrigin must appear here. That is what keeps this gate meaningful while the list below is empty. Without it, the first onion-only route could ship unregistered and the gate would report success over an endpoint it had never looked at.
resting_state_comment: ONION_INGRESS_MAC_KEY is absent in production, so classifyOrigin returns 'clearnet' for every request and every endpoint listed here refuses for everyone on every network. That is the correct resting state, not an outage: the operated onion origin does not exist yet, and a life-safety flow that quietly worked over clearnet would be worse than one that is honestly closed.
why_field_comment: Each entry carries a `why` of at least 40 characters explaining what pairing or correlation the onion requirement defeats for THAT endpoint. Same lesson as platform_key.why in sensitive-endpoints.json: a registry whose entries carry no reasoning becomes a list nobody rereads, and the next person removes an entry because they cannot see what it was for.
